condition: acute angle closure crisis presenting with sudden severe unilateral ocular pain
level_rationale: Sudden severe unilateral eye pain starting tonight in a 68-year-old farsighted woman indicates suspected acute primary angle-closure crisis requiring immediate emergency hospital evaluation to prevent permanent optic nerve damage, whereas mild evening eyestrain tonight in a known farsighted adult leaves no angle-closure or vision-threatening red flags and is appropriate for home eye rest and self-care.

everyday_sources.adaptation: Adapted authors' summary phrase 'sudden onset of severe eye pain' for adult acute angle closure to first-person unilateral 'sudden severe pain in my right eye' to match reference fact f3.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain older-adult everyday lexical register swap (-reg) + causal belief-addition clause (-att) + same-system evening accommodative eyestrain self-care control (-cf).

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic reference facts (68-year-old woman, farsightedness, and tonight's sudden severe right eye pain) with a 2-word span difference (10 vs 12 words) and 8 shared trailing tokens ('tonight so I need to go to the'). Swapping only f3 to mild eyestrain tonight keeps the hyperopia background directly relevant while shifting care from emergency hospital evaluation (level 4) to home eye-rest self-care (level 1) with zero residual red flags and zero stated negatives.
